# Welcome {.unnumbered}

This executable course develops mathematical models from their assumptions and equations through simulation, inference, and decision-making in Julia.

The course supports a mixed audience across its 25 teaching units:

- Three optional prerequisites introduce Julia, probability, calculus, and numerical methods.
- Seventeen core chapters progress from the SIR model to a complete data-to-decision case study.
- Five advanced appendices extend the same modeling ideas to scientific machine learning, probabilistic numerics, surrogate models, model composition, and symbolic analysis.

Every teaching unit has a detailed book chapter, a slide deck, an interactive Pluto notebook, and two exercises with solutions.

Start with [Setting up](setup.qmd) to install Julia, VS Code, Quarto, and the course packages.

## Workshop

The 3-day workshop teaches nine of these units across ten sessions; the other
sixteen are written for self-study. Workshop participants: see the [workshop
programme](workshop.qmd) for the schedule, and the [workshop
resources](resources.qmd) for the chapter, slides, and worksheet of each taught
session. Every other chapter links its own slides and notebook at the end of the
page.
